description.text: We are North America’s largest “do-it-yourself” moving and storage operator through our subsidiary U-Haul International, Inc. (“U-Haul”). U-Haul is synonymous with “do-it-yourself” moving and storage and is a leader in supplying products and services to help people move and store their household and commercial goods. Our primary service objective is to “provide a better and better product and service to more and more people at a lower and lower cost.” Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms “U-Haul Holding Company,” “Company,” “we,” “us,” or “our” refer to U-Haul Holding Company, a Nevada corporation, and all of its legal subsidiaries, on a consolidated basis. We were founded in 1945 as a sole proprietorship under the name "U-Haul Trailer Rental Company" and have rented trailers ever since. Starting in 1959, we rented trucks on a one-way and in-town basis exclusively through independent U-Haul dealers. In 1973, we began developing our network of U-Haul managed retail stores, through which we rent our trucks and trailers, self-storage units and portable moving and storage units and sell moving and self-storage products and services to complement our independent dealer network. We rent our distinctive orange and white U-Haul trucks and trailers, and orange door self-storage units, through a network of over 2,400 Company-operated retail moving stores and over 23,000 independent U-Haul dealers.

about.description_short: Founded in 1945, U-Haul is the No. 1 choice of do-it-yourself movers with more than 25,000 rental locations across all 50 states and 10 Canadian provinces. The U-Haul app makes it easy for customers to use U-Haul Truck Share 24/7 to access trucks anytime through the self-dispatch and -return options on their smartphones with our patented Live Verify technology. Our customers' patronage has enabled the U-Haul fleet to grow to approximately 207,600 trucks, 136,500 trailers and 43,200 towing devices. U-Haul, which offers rate transparency to self-storage customers through its 1-Year Price Lock, is the third largest storage operator in North America with 1,147,300 rentable storage units and 100.3 million square feet of self-storage space at owned and managed facilities. U-Haul is the top retailer of propane in the U.S. and the largest installer of permanent trailer hitches in the automotive aftermarket industry.

analysis_md:
# UHAL — U-Haul Holding Company
Engine 5.4 pass-1 run, 2026-10-18. In scope (market cap $11.180B at $57.02, nasdaq_quote_api — key_numbers.md).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The parent of U-Haul International (DIY truck/trailer rental and self-storage, the Moving & Storage segment), Amerco Real Estate, Repwest (property & casualty insurance) and Oxford Life Insurance. SIC 7510 (fundamentals.json profile). FY2026 total revenues $6,037,819,000 (fundamentals.json, Revenues tag — see the BASIS_BREAK flag below for why the engine's revenue series differs), of which the 10-K consolidating schedule attributes $3,811,921k to self-moving equipment rentals and $972,427k to self-storage. Founded 1945; Shoen-family controlled, with two share classes — Voting Common Stock (UHAL) and Series N Non-Voting Common Stock (UHAL.B) — sharing earnings under the two-class method (10-K Note 4).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,794,584,000; capex (purchases of property, plant and equipment) $3,154,325,000; SBC $0 — by filing override, see OVERRIDES.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: −$1,359,741,000 = −$6.93/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-6.93). FY2025 −$1,998,052,000 and FY2024 −$1,540,142,000 on the same definition (financials_history.csv totals). OE-positive years in the last 5: **0/5**.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base, the median of the last 3 fiscal years: −$7.85/share** (key_numbers.md). No TTM pin was used as the base, but ttm.py was run and agrees in sign and scale (below), so the median is not a stale-year artifact.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, financials_history.csv): $83,128,000 in FY2026, $367,090,000 in FY2025, $628,707,000 in FY2024 — i.e. exactly net income in each year, because the ΔNWC leg is not tagged. This definition caps capex at depreciation ($1,183,133,000 in FY2026), which flatters a fleet business whose replacement purchases are its largest cash cost; even taken at face value it is $83,128,000 against an $11.180B market cap. The conservative definition is the honest base here, and both definitions are far below any hurdle.
- **TTM check (ttm.py, through Q1 FY2027 ended 2026-06-30):** OCF: FY $1,794,584,000 − prior YTD $598,376,000 + current YTD $630,277,000 = **TTM $1,826,485,000**. Capex: FY $3,154,325,000 − prior YTD $916,571,000 + current YTD $822,362,000 = **TTM $3,060,116,000**. SBC: **$0** on all three legs (override-filled, ttm.json overrides_used). Shares (current-YTD): **195,869,719** — the count has begun to fall under the buyback the company reported in Q1 FY2027 ($48M of repurchases in the quarter, per the Q1 FY2027 results coverage). **TTM OE total −$1,233,631,000 → −$6.30/share** (ttm.json). Still deeply negative; no base choice rescues this name.
- Latest quarter (Q1 FY2027, Business Wire release 2026-08-05): consolidated revenue $1,682,027k, +3.2% vs the prior-year quarter (self-storage +6.8%, self-moving equipment rentals +2.8% on the release's product table); net earnings available to common shareholders $122,929k, down from $142,331k — revenue growth with margin compression, the same pattern as FY2026.
- Balance sheet (key_numbers.md / dcf_numbers.json): net debt $7.005B on a TOTAL:LongTermDebt basis. The 10-K consolidating balance sheet at March 31, 2026 shows notes, loans and finance leases payable, net of $8,083,374k against cash and equivalents of $1,120,147k — consistent with the engine's figure. This is fleet-and-real-estate debt secured by the asset base (PP&E, net $16,380,445,000, financials_history.csv), not an unsecured blow-up, but it is large against zero conservative OE.

## OVERRIDES — sbc and shares (both kind "filing", both unblock the tier)
- **The gaps:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP: sbc, shares` — no tier. Both were resolved inside the bounded authority (step 8a: figures from the company's own filings), and make_score.py records both as `unblocks_tier: YES`.
- **sbc_override = $0.** The FY2026 10-K's Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. F-6) enumerate every operating reconciliation item for FY2024–FY2026 — depreciation, premium amortization, debt-issuance amortization, interest credited to policyholders, disposal gains/losses, deferred taxes, working-capital changes — and reconcile exactly to reported operating cash flow ($1,794,584k / $1,454,429k / $1,452,756k) with no share-based compensation line; the terms "share-based" and "stock-based" appear nowhere in the filing, and companyfacts carries no SBC fact for CIK 4457 in any year. There is no SBC expense to subtract. The override is flagged out-of-band by construction (no filed value exists to band against); judgment.json carries the ack_reason, and the engine recorded `ack_reason_present: true`. Measured impact (key_numbers.md): base OE/share −$7.85 with and without the override — the value is $0, so nothing moves; the effect is binary (without it there is no tier).
- **shares_override = 196,077,880.** Note 4 (Earnings Per Share, pp. F-17/F-18) states weighted average shares on a "Basic and diluted" basis for both classes: Voting Common 19,607,788 + Series N Non-Voting 176,470,092 = 196,077,880 total, identical in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024. Companyfacts tags only the basic series at that combined count, which tripped the v5.4 basic-only gap rule; the filing itself certifies the same count as diluted. Measured impact: none on any per-share figure (the engine already used this count as its fallback); it certifies the denominator as diluted.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate; a real network earning shrinking returns
Justification: dominant DIY moving network — 24,000+ locations, >50% DIY share, a fleet larger than the top three rivals combined and the #3 self-storage operator in North America — but a capital-intensive, price-compared rental business whose measured returns have eroded (ROIC proxy 24.5% → 2.2%, operating margin 21.7% → 7.2%, FY2017 → FY2026, fundamentals.json), so the moat is real but no longer earning wide-moat returns.
- FOR: location density no rival matches (24,000+ company + independent-dealer locations vs roughly 2,500 for Penske — convenience is the purchase criterion in DIY moving); scale (~207,600 trucks, larger than the top three competitors combined, >50% DIY share); brand default since 1945 feeding direct/app demand (Truck Share 24/7); the self-storage flywheel (#3 in North America, ~100.3M sq ft, attached to the moving funnel; storage revenue +8.3% in FY2026 with revenue per occupied foot rising); dealer network expanding reach on other people's capital and vertical integration (fleet manufacturing/repair, propane, hitches) supporting availability and cost.
- AGAINST: measured returns contradict a wide moat (below); commodity, price-compared purchase with zero switching cost (Penske, Avis Budget, Enterprise); capital intensity — FY2026 capex $3,154,325,000 against depreciation $1,183,133,000 (financials_history.csv), the network must be continuously re-bought; post-COVID over-expansion (FY2026 fleet depreciation up $186.6M and disposal losses $117.6M per the FY2026 results release; management conceded in Q1 FY2027 that new storage units are completing faster than they fill); Shoen-family control, $114.1M of FY2026 related-party costs (10-K), and the $7.005B net debt load.
- **ROIC / margin evidence (fundamentals.json, roic_proxy series):** 24.5% (FY2017), 9.8%, 6.7%, 4.7%, 8.7%, 13.5% (FY2022), 10.4%, 6.1%, 4.0%, **2.2% (FY2026)** — a decade-long slide from well above the cost of capital to below it, with only the pandemic moving boom interrupting it. Operating margin over the same span: 21.7% → 7.2%, including 17.4% → 12.3% → 7.2% across FY2024–FY2026. The fundamentals.json "gross margin" (~95.9%) is **not** a usable margin for this filer: its COGS leg captures only product-sales cost while rental operating costs sit in operating expenses, so operating margin is the margin line quoted here. A moat above 5 would need ROIC evidence this history does not provide.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. (Academic here — see DCF.)

## DCF — Tier F: no scenario table exists, by design
The engine emits no scenario IVs or IRRs for this name: the normalized base is negative, so there is no owner's-earnings path to discount. Probabilities were left at the defaults 10/25/30/25/10 and offsets/multipliers at the engine defaults (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp; 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25) and are recorded in dcf_numbers.json inputs, but they multiply a negative base and produce nothing quotable — no figure is invented here to fill the table.
- **Growth sanity check (required even though it cannot change the tier):** the engine's growth blend is 0.67% (key_numbers.md), built from a corrupted revenue series — rev CAGR 5y −30.04% is the revenue-tag break resolved under BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT below, not a real decline. On the filer's own total-revenue series (fundamentals.json), revenue grew from $4,541,985,000 (FY2021) to $6,037,819,000 (FY2026), FY2026 itself +3.6% (the key_numbers.md latest rev YoY of 3.60% is correct on both bases), and Q1 FY2027 printed +3.2%. Scenario starts around the blend (base 0.67%, bull +5.67pp over it) sit *below* the +3.2–3.6% the company just printed; the written reason is that it does not matter — every scenario multiplies a negative OE base, and the tier is F under any growth start. If this name's OE ever turns positive, the growth inputs must be rebuilt on the Revenues-tag series, not this blend.
- **Hurdle-clearing price:** none exists on this model. With a negative base OE/share (−$7.85 normalized, −$6.93 latest FY, −$6.30 TTM — every basis negative), no positive purchase price produces a 15% owner's-earnings IRR; the question the model answers is not "how cheap is cheap enough" but "when does fleet capex fall back inside operating cash flow."

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:sbc / DATA_GAP:shares** (preliminary run): resolved by the two filing overrides above; the final run's data_gap is empty and both overrides are recorded in dcf_numbers.json and the registry with measured (zero) impact and `unblocks_tier: true`.
- **DILUTION** (preliminary run, "share count growing 77.8%/yr"): an artifact, now gone from the final run (share count CAGR 0.00%, key_numbers.md). The preliminary history mixed denominators — pre-FY2023 basic facts carried only the 19,607,788 Voting shares, while FY2024–FY2026 carry the combined 196,077,880 after the October–December 2022 creation of the Series N class (a 9-for-1 stock dividend of non-voting shares to voting holders). No shares were issued to outsiders; the combined weighted count has been flat at 196,077,880 for three fiscal years, and the current-YTD count (195,869,719, ttm.json) is *falling* under buybacks.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: a revenue-tag break, not a business break. From FY2022 the engine's preferred tag (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) captures only a ~$0.7B revenue sub-line ($761,453,000 in FY2026), while the filer's total revenues sit under the Revenues tag ($6,037,819,000 in FY2026, fundamentals.json) — hence the fake −30.04% 5-yr CAGR and the apparent >60% revenue drop in financials_history.csv from FY2022. No divestiture, M&A or restatement caused it (the insurance subsidiaries are consolidated throughout). Total revenues grew in FY2025 (+3.6% on the fundamentals series: $5,828,665,000 after $5,625,674,000) and FY2026 (+3.6% to $6,037,819,000); growth inputs must not straddle the FY2022 tag switch, as discussed in the DCF section. The OE series itself (OCF, capex, NI tags) is unaffected by the break.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (NI vs OCF differ by >40% in 2024, 2025, 2026): structural fleet depreciation, not a one-off. The gap is the non-cash reconciliation in the 10-K cash-flow statement — depreciation of $817,889k / $971,933k / $1,183,133k (FY2024/25/26) plus deferred income taxes ($98,379k / $41,907k / $52,045k in the consolidating schedules) and disposal results swinging from a $153,958k gain (FY2024) to a $103,888k loss (FY2026). Net income is the *smaller* number every year precisely because the fleet's depreciation is real and growing; the OCF-based conservative OE used throughout is not contaminated by the divergence — if anything the divergence understates the problem, since capex runs well ahead of even that depreciation.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (no diluted count filed for 2017–2022): noted — those history years use the basic/dei counts in the shares_tag column of financials_history.csv and, per the DILUTION resolution above, the pre-FY2023 counts are on the voting-only basis, so per-share history before FY2024 is not comparable with the combined-basis recent years. The base window (FY2024–FY2026) is on one consistent, override-certified diluted basis.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:shares**: see OVERRIDES — sources, reasons, ack (sbc) and measured impacts are all in judgment.json / dcf_numbers.json / key_numbers.md, not just here.
- No SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH flag fired and none is warranted for the headline business: Moving & Storage is an operating rental business the OE model fits (badly for the company, but fittingly). The two insurance subsidiaries are consolidated noise at this scale and, if anything, their investment income flatters OCF; they are not the reason for the F.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the *method range*, and unusually it does not span the hurdle: conservative OE is negative on the median (−$7.85/share), the latest FY (−$6.93/share) and the TTM (−$6.30/share); the maintenance definition is positive but only $83,128,000 in FY2026 against an $11.180B market cap. Every defensible base sits below every hurdle — the range runs F to, at the most generous reading, a deep D. Tier F by numbers stands without an override.
- Why the model is this harsh, and why it is not obviously wrong: U-Haul's capex line is mostly rental-fleet purchases — the product itself. The engine charges gross purchases ($3,154,325,000 in FY2026); the 10-K also reports proceeds from sales of property, plant and equipment of $710,286k in FY2026, an order smaller than the purchase program, so even a net-of-disposals view leaves fleet investment far above the $1,794,584,000 of operating cash flow. Management's own Q1 FY2027 guidance — a reduction of more than $500M in net fleet investment over the remaining quarters — is an admission that the fleet was over-bought; if that cut lands and depreciation rolls off, OE can inflect. That is a forecast, not a filing, and pass 1 scores filings.
- What would change the verdict: two consecutive fiscal years of capex inside OCF (the FY2027 fleet-investment cut, delivered), storage occupancy recovering as the development pipeline (11.7M NRSF in development or pending at FY2026, per the FY2026 release) leases up instead of diluting, and ROIC climbing back above the cost of capital. Until then the market is pricing the asset base ($16,380,445,000 of net PP&E, much of it land and storage real estate) and a normalized-earnings hope — neither of which this owner's-earnings screen credits.
- Governance/ownership note for any future position: family control, the two-class structure (the voting line is the thin one — 19,607,788 shares), and related-party arrangements are permanent features, not catalysts.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier_by_numbers F, f_subtype no_cash_generation — OCF − capex is not positive on the last-3-FY window; no tier override)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the filing arithmetic — both gaps cured with filing-proven overrides whose measured impact is zero; medium on the model fit for a fleet-rental business, which is why the maintenance-definition cross-check is documented above rather than suppressed)
- One-liner: Dominant moving-and-storage network, moat 5/10, but no positive conservative owner's earnings at any point in the last 5 years — fleet capex swallows operating cash flow (base OE -$7.85/share, latest FY -$6.93/share), so Tier F at $57.02; it clears no hurdle on this model and even the maintenance definition (FY2026 OE $83,128k) is under 1% of the $11.18B market cap.
